name: Cipher Digital

logo.source: cipherdigital.com header logo (inline SVG, Cipher Digital wordmark and dot mark)

description: Cipher Digital (formerly Cipher Mining) is turning a bitcoin miner into a data-center landlord. Until now all of its revenue has been bitcoin mined at its Odessa, Texas site (and at Black Pearl until February 2026); in the latest quarter that was $24.8 million, down from $43.6 million, with an operating loss of $78.5 million. The change in business is contracted but not yet earning: it signed long-term high-performance-computing leases with Fluidstack (Google backstops its payments) for 300 gross MW at Barber Lake and with Amazon Web Services for a 15-year, 300 gross MW lease at Black Pearl, with first capacity and rent starting in the second half of 2026. It pays for this with large debt raises: about $3.2 billion in 2025, an $810 million secured note in June 2026 and $850 million of zero-coupon convertible notes in October 2026. The site portfolio is about 5.3 GW across 11 sites, most of it still in the interconnection queue.

businessLines.name: Bitcoin mining (Odessa; Black Pearl until February 2026)
businessLines.how: Pays a fixed price for power, runs miners and contributes hashrate to mining pools in exchange for a proportional share of bitcoin block rewards and transaction fees; profit depends on the bitcoin price versus a 2.8 c/kWh power cost, and surplus power is resold to the Texas grid.
businessLines.description: Runs bitcoin miners on a 207 MW wholly owned site in Odessa, Texas supplied by a fixed-price Luminant power contract (2.8 c/kWh since October 2025, take-or-pay for at least 66.7% of capacity, to at least July 2027), and until February 2026 on a 300 MW site at Black Pearl (Wink, Texas). Sold its 49% interests in three 40 MW joint-venture sites to Canaan on 2026-02-19.

businessLines.name: HPC data-center leasing (Barber Lake, Black Pearl; not yet revenue-producing)
businessLines.how: Intends to collect long-term fixed rent from hyperscaler or hyperscaler-backed tenants for powered, turnkey data-center space (a landlord model, with project-level non-recourse debt); rent starts per phase after delivery.
businessLines.description: Develops, builds and will operate turnkey data centers leased to hyperscaler-grade tenants under long-term gross modified leases: Barber Lake near Colorado City, Texas (300 MW gross, all to Fluidstack with a Google backstop of Fluidstack's obligations; Phase I 244 MW, Phase II 56 MW) and Black Pearl near Wink, Texas (300 gross MW, 15-year lease with Amazon Web Services). A third HPC lease is referred to in the Q2 2026 10-Q ('leases at three of our data centers') but the site was not identified in the text read.

revenue.note: No lease revenue yet. Q2 2026 revenue was all bitcoin mining. Black Pearl first capacity delivery was accelerated to 2026-07-31 (lease amended 2026-07-24); Barber Lake Phase I delivery targeted 2026-09-30.
